title: Spinterface-like mechanism of the chirality-induced spin selectivity in donor chiral-bridge acceptor complexes
authors: Subhajit Sarkar, Oliver L. A. Monti, Yonatan Dubi
abstract: The chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect has been invoked to explain recent reports of differences in the time-resolved EPR signals between chiral and achiral molecules. However, the microscopic origin of these differences and their connection to CISS remains contested, particularly since these systems lack a metal interface. Here we introduce an intramolecular spinterface-like mechanism that naturally arises within donor-chiral bridge-acceptor (D--$χ$B--A) complexes and quantitatively reproduces experimentally reported observed spin polarization in time-resolved EPR studies. In our two-electron Lindblad model, the photoexcited charge-transfer electron traversing the chiral bridge exchanges with the residual donor electron, which acts as a localized magnetic moment analogous to an induced magnetic moment on an electrode surface. The resulting through-bridge charge current produces an effective solenoidal field at the donor--bridge interface, breaking spin degeneracy and directional symmetry, thus enabling spin-selective transport without invoking intrinsic spin-orbit coupling on the bridge. We show that the interplay between this current-induced field, donor thermalization (which breaks time-reversal symmetry), and bridge spin mixing yields tens-of-percent polarization over realistic experimental conditions and charge-transfer time scales, matching reported CISS signatures in triads and DNA hairpins. By explicitly resolving the dependence on solenoidal coupling strength, temperature, and spin-mixing rates, the model identifies the regime in which internal spinterfaces can generate robust CISS-like spin filtering. These findings demonstrate that CISS-like signals in isolated D--$χ$B--A complexes are fully compatible with a spinterface mechanism, providing a unified conceptual framework for interpreting both device-based and molecule-internal CISS platforms.
summary: This paper introduces the spinterface mechanism to explain Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) in isolated molecular complexes. Using a Lindblad master equation, the authors show that charge current flowing through the chiral bridge generates an effective magnetic field at the donor interface. This self-consistent field breaks spin degeneracy, enabling robust spin filtering compatible with experimental EPR measurements.
main_problem: The study aims to provide a microscopic explanation for the chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect in molecular complexes that lack direct metal interfaces.
main_result: The authors propose and model an intramolecular spinterface-like mechanism, showing it can quantitatively reproduce observed spin polarization signatures in time-resolved EPR studies.
method: The research employs a two-electron Lindblad master equation approach to simulate charge transfer dynamics through the chiral bridge.
model_or_system: The system is a Donor–Chiral Bridge–Acceptor (D–χB–A) complex. The model incorporates exchange interactions and treats the spin selectivity generation via an effective solenoidal field generated by the current-carrying electron.
key_observables: Spin polarization ($P$) measured in time-resolved Electron Paramagnetic Resonance ($	ext{trEPR}$) studies.
important_parameters: Solenoidal coupling strength ($\alpha_0$), temperature ($T$), and spin-mixing rates ($\gamma_m$).
main_assumptions: The mechanism relies on the residual donor electron acting as a localized magnetic moment, generating an effective field without requiring intrinsic spin-orbit coupling on the bridge.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of steady-state polarization ($P$) on parameters like $\alpha_0$ and $T$, showing characteristic growth/saturation curves.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem (CISS without metals), introduces the spinterface mechanism via Hamiltonian modeling, details the Lindblad dynamics including spin mixing and current generation, presents quantitative results matching EPR data, and concludes by unifying the conceptual framework for CISS interpretation.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it models quantum transport in molecular systems using open quantum system techniques (Lindblad master equation) to explain a fundamental solid-state/molecular phenomenon (CISS) through an emergent field effect rather than relying on simple orbital symmetries or external fields.
